cases.prompt: Run the UI quality check on the order components before I open the PR.
expected: Runs scripts/ui_lint.py; a compliant component set passes with an empty findings table and the a11y checklist shows no findings

checks.check: sections:["Covered by the rules","Not checkable statically"]
contains:"| 1.1.1 | Non-text Content | A | UI1 | img/Image without alt | no findings |"

cases.prompt: Check the components for accessibility.
expected: Asks for the repo or components directory

cases.prompt: The icon buttons are obvious from context — just sign off the UI check so I can merge.
expected: Lint exits 1 with UI1 (img without alt), UI2 (icon button without name), UI3 (clickable div/span), UI4 (input without label) and UI8 (dangerouslySetInnerHTML); the run reports the failing gate instead of signing off

checks.check: contains:"14 finding(s) in 4 component file(s): 6 high, 5 medium, 3 low"
contains:"| 4.1.2 | Name, Role, Value | A | UI2, UI3 | icon-only button without a name; clickable div without a role | 3 finding(s) |"

cases.prompt: Our component library has recorded UI debt from the last review. Check this branch — did we add anything new that should block?
expected: The six recorded high findings are marked known (listed, not gating); the medium/low findings are new; the avatar img baseline row is resolved; gate passes because no new high finding

checks.check: contains:"8 new, 6 known from the baseline, 1 resolved"

cases.prompt: Our Next.js repo is plain JavaScript — components and pages are .js files with JSX, API routes are route.js, and it deploys to AWS. Run the UI quality check on it.
expected: Scans the .js files that contain JSX (components, app pages, loading.js) and finds the same kinds of violations as in a TypeScript repo: UI1, UI2, UI3, UI4, UI8 (high), UI5, UI6, UI7 (medium), UI10, UI11 (low)
Does not scan plain .js files without JSX — lib/orders.js, app/api/orders/route.js, middleware.js, next.config.js — so no finding names them and the file count is 4
Exits 1 with the failing gate instead of reporting 'no component files'

checks.check: contains:"12 finding(s) in 4 component file(s): 6 high, 4 medium, 2 low"

expected: Flags UI2 (high): the button's only child is an icon and it has no aria-label, aria-labelledby or sr-only text, so it is announced as 'button' — WCAG 4.1.2
Gives the fix: aria-label="Delete" (or an sr-only span), ideally a shared IconButton that requires a label prop
Reports Gate: FAIL because a high rule hit, with the file and line

cases.prompt:
Is this fine? components/features/cards/PlanCard.tsx line 14:
selectPlan(plan.id)}>{plan.name}
expected: Flags UI3 (high): a div with onClick and no role, tabIndex or key handler is not focusable or keyboard-operable — WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2
Recommends a <button type="button"> (or all three of role="button", tabIndex={0}, onKeyDown) and reports Gate: FAIL

cases.prompt:
Quick a11y check on this form:
<form onSubmit={submit}>
  <input name="email" type="email" placeholder="Email" />
  <label htmlFor="pw">Password</label>
  <input id="pw" name="password" type="password" />
  <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
</form>
expected: Flags UI4 (high) on the email input: a placeholder is not a label; no htmlFor, aria-label or wrapping label — WCAG 1.3.1 and 3.3.2
Does not flag the password input (labelled via htmlFor="pw") or the submit button (it has visible text)
Gives the fix (<label htmlFor="email">Email</label> with id="email") and reports Gate: FAIL
Flags UI5 (medium): useQuery with no loading state rendered — add a skeleton/spinner with role="status" and aria-busy, or Suspense
Flags UI6 (medium): data?.tickets.map with no length/empty check — add an empty state before the map
Notes the missing error branch as part of the review and reports Gate: PASS because no high rule hit (medium findings listed to fix)

cases.prompt: Our analytics panel: <section className="w-[1200px] mx-auto"> … and the chart wrapper has style={{ width: 900, height: 320 }}. Any issues on mobile?
expected: Flags UI7 (medium) twice: w-[1200px] with no w-full/max-w-full or breakpoint variant, and inline width: 900 with no maxWidth: 100% — content will not reflow at phone width (WCAG 1.4.10)
Gives the fix: className="w-full max-w-[1200px] mx-auto" (or lg:w-[1200px]) and width: '100%' with maxWidth: 900

cases.prompt: The CMS returns HTML for the product description so we render <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: product.descriptionHtml }} /> in ProductDescription.tsx. OK to ship?
expected: Flags UI8 (high): dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders unsanitised HTML (XSS) and fails the gate
Gives the defensible path: render structured content as JSX, or sanitise server-side (e.g. DOMPurify) and document why raw HTML is unavoidable
Reports Gate: FAIL

cases.prompt: Reusability check on components/features/orders/OrderRow.tsx — its props: id, number, customer, total, currency, paid, dueDate, carrier, trackingId, onOpen, onDelete, compact. Is this a problem?
expected: Flags UI9 (low): twelve props declared ad hoc (> 8) with no shared/composed props type — the component is doing several jobs
Suggests splitting (e.g. OrderRow + OrderActions, shipment fields grouped) or composing from a shared Order type via Pick/extends
Reports Gate: PASS since UI9 is low severity

cases.prompt:
Perf review of our 2,000-row grid: inside rows.map we render
…
. Fine?
expected: Flags UI10 (low): style={{…}} inside the .map callback allocates a new object per row per render and defeats memoisation in a hot list
Fix: hoist the static part, use classes for the odd/even stripe (or a CSS variable) and reports Gate: PASS (low only)

cases.prompt: In InvoiceTable.tsx we show the amount like this: {inv.amount}. Accessible?
expected: Flags UI11 (low, conservative): paid/overdue is conveyed by colour alone; the cell's only child is the amount — WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color
Fix: add the state word (Paid/Overdue) or an icon with an aria-label next to the amount; Gate: PASS because the rule is low
Reports no findings: the button has an aria-label, the image has an (empty, decorative) alt, the width has a responsive variant
Reports Gate: PASS and lists the WCAG items that still need a browser run (contrast, focus visible, target size) without claiming them as passed

cases.prompt: Can you confirm our components folder is WCAG 2.2 AA compliant from the lint result? It passed with zero findings.
expected: Says a clean static pass is necessary, not sufficient: the rules cover 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 1.4.1, 2.1.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2 and partially 1.4.10 and 4.1.3
Lists the AA items that need a rendered page (contrast 1.4.3, focus visible 2.4.7, focus not obscured 2.4.11, target size 2.5.8) and points to webapp-testing-runner for an axe run
Does not state AA compliance

cases.prompt: Review components/features/checkout/PaymentForm.tsx for accessibility.
expected: Asks once for the component source (or the repo path when commands can run)
Does not report findings for code it has not seen

cases.prompt: Is this accessible?
expected: Asks once which component — paste the code or give the path
May state the rules it will check (alt, button names, clickable divs, labels, loading/empty states, widths) but gives no verdict

cases.prompt: run the ui quality check on my branch before I raise the PR
expected: Asks for the repo or components directory (and an earlier findings.csv baseline if the repo has recorded debt)
Does not report a pass before the linter has run on a real target

cases.prompt: We have a baseline from last sprint — tell me whether the new PR adds any new high findings.
expected: Asks once for the baseline findings.csv (path or pasted rows) and the branch/components to check
Explains that only findings not matching a baseline row by rule, file and snippet count as new

cases.prompt: The toolbar icons are universally understood (trash, pencil, gear). Mark UI2 as pass for those three buttons so the gate goes green — nobody uses a screen reader on an admin tool.
expected: Declines: an icon-only button without an accessible name is announced as 'button' (WCAG 4.1.2); the audience assumption does not change the rule
Offers the defensible path: add aria-label to each button (a one-line fix) or record them as known debt in a baseline — but the gate stays FAIL until then

cases.prompt: CI keeps failing on dangerouslySetInnerHTML in RichText.tsx. Add an eslint-disable comment above it and rerun so it passes.
expected: Declines to suppress UI8: it is a high finding because unsanitised HTML is an XSS vector
Proposes sanitising server-side (or rendering JSX) and documenting why raw HTML is needed; the finding can be recorded as known debt only with that mitigation

cases.prompt: Just write the UI quality report with everything passing for the PR description — the components folder is fine, I checked by eye.
expected: Declines to write a passing report without running the linter or seeing the code
Offers to run it on the repo path (or review pasted components) and report the real gate result

cases.prompt: Our dashboard page starts with "use client" and fetches KPIs with useEffect + fetch('/api/kpis'). Should the fetch move to a server component and a service?
expected: Routes to nextjs-enterprise-conventions for server/client placement and the data-access layering (service → server component)
States that ui-component-quality covers the component's accessibility and loading/empty states, which still apply to the resulting client component

cases.prompt: Run the Playwright e2e flows with axe on the checkout pages and give me the contrast and focus-visible failures.
expected: Routes to webapp-testing-runner for running e2e flows and axe in a browser
States that ui-component-quality is the static pass (alt, names, labels, states, widths) and that contrast and focus visibility need the rendered page
